name: HTML
tagline: The structural scaffolding of the worldwide web.
timeTravelLog: Discovered in 1991 at CERN by Tim Berners-Lee. Designed to encode human knowledge and send it across the dimensions of the digital space-time continuum.
overview: HTML is the standard markup language for creating web pages. It defines the structure of a web page using elements and tags, serving as the skeleton upon which CSS styles and JavaScript logic are applied.

syllabus.title: Module 3: Wormhole Navigation (Anchors & Hyperlinks)
syllabus.desc: Creating hyperlink portals to travel between pages and external systems.
syllabus.content: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks. The href attribute defines the destination — it can be a full URL, a relative page path, or even a section ID on the current page using a # hash. Using target="_blank" opens the link in a new tab, like opening a parallel dimension.
syllabus.codeExample: Jump to NASA Portal ↗ About Sector Go to Systems Section
syllabus.interactiveTip: Always add rel="noopener noreferrer" when using target="_blank" to prevent security vulnerabilities from malicious third-party pages!

syllabus.title: Module 4: Containers & Compartments (Divs vs Spans)
syllabus.desc: Grouping page elements using block and inline structural wrappers.
syllabus.content: To group elements and build compartments, we use <div> — a block-level box that occupies the full row width — and <span> — an inline tag for highlighting small runs of text without disrupting flow. Both are neutral containers styled completely by CSS.
syllabus.codeExample:
Subsystem 4

Status: ONLINE
syllabus.interactiveTip: Think of divs as storage boxes (block) and spans as sticky labels (inline). Never put block-level elements like <div> or <h1> inside a <span>!

syllabus.title: Module 5: Semantic Architecture (Header, Footer, Main, Section, Article)
syllabus.desc: Writing meaningful HTML that communicates structure to both humans and machines.
syllabus.content: Semantic elements carry meaning beyond just visual layout. <header> marks site-wide navigation decks, <main> wraps the core content, <section> groups related topics, <article> represents standalone content, and <footer> holds base coordinates. These improve SEO rankings and screen-reader accessibility dramatically.
syllabus.codeExample:
[ NAVIGATION LINKS ]

Mission Report

Status: All systems nominal.

Coordinates: 9.9312 N, 76.2673 E
syllabus.interactiveTip: Semantic HTML improves search engine ranking by giving crawlers exact context about your page structure. Always prefer semantic elements over generic divs!

syllabus.title: Module 6: Input Arrays (Forms, Inputs, Labels, Buttons)
syllabus.desc: Capturing user intelligence through interactive form field arrays.
syllabus.content: HTML Forms (<form>) collect user data and transmit it via HTTP. Inside forms, <input> elements capture text, numbers, checkboxes, radios, and passwords. <label> tags improve accessibility by linking visible text to input controls. <button> submits or triggers form actions.
syllabus.codeExample:
<form action="/send" method="POST">
  <label for="pilot-id">Pilot Code:</label>
  <input type="text" id="pilot-id" name="pilot" placeholder="Enter ID...">
  
  <label for="clearance">Clearance Level:</label>
  <select id="clearance" name="level">
    <option value="alpha">ALPHA</option>
    <option value="omega">OMEGA</option>
  </select>
  
  <button type="submit">TRANSMIT</button>
</form>
syllabus.interactiveTip: Always pair <label> elements with <input> using matching 'for' and 'id' attributes. This allows clicking the label to focus the input field!

syllabus.title: Module 7: Meta Telemetry (Head Tags, Favicons & SEO)
syllabus.desc: Configuring hidden control signals in the <head> for browsers and search engines.
syllabus.content: The <head> element is the invisible mission control of every HTML page. It contains <title> (the browser tab text), <meta> tags for descriptions, keywords and viewport, <link> tags for stylesheets and favicons, and structured data scripts. These signals directly influence how your page appears in search results.
syllabus.codeExample:
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Mission Control | JES-007</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Elite temporal engineering portfolio.">
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/style.css">
</head>
syllabus.interactiveTip: The meta viewport tag is critical for mobile responsiveness! Without it, mobile browsers render your page at desktop width and scale it down, making text tiny.

quiz.question: What does HTML stand for?
quiz.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language — the standard language used to structure and define the content of web pages.

quiz.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?
quiz.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks. Its 'href' attribute specifies the destination URL or page path.

quiz.question: Which semantic element represents the primary content area of a page?
quiz.explanation: <main> is the semantic element that wraps the dominant, unique content of the page — there should only be one per document.

quest.title: Quest: Code a Galactic Dashboard
quest.challenge: Build a complete page structure with semantic tags, a form, an image, and proper meta information in the head.
instructions: 1. Add a <header> with an <h1> title for your spaceship.
2. Add a <main> section containing an <article> with a mission description.
3. Add an tag showing a space photo from any public URL.
4. Create a <form> with a text input for pilot name and a submit button.
5. Wrap everything properly and verify your semantic structure.
